MAJAZ:v2p227/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p227/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p227/r2.claim: فتول عنهم means turn away from and leave them; Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḍamḍam's poetry uses ولى of a horseman departing.

MAJAZ:v2p227/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p227/r3.speaker: حصين بن ضمضم
MAJAZ:v2p227/r3.claim: Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḍamḍam's verse describes a horseman leaving his companions and escaping.
MAJAZ:v2p227/r3.anchor: قال حصين بن ضمضم أما بنو عبس فإن هجينهم

NAHHAS:v4p249/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r14.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p249/r14.claim: Mujahid glosses فأعرض as turn away; the implied instruction is to turn away until God’s order about them came, namely the command to fight them.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r14.anchor: قال مجاهد أي أعرض والتقدير أعرض عنهم حتى يأتيك أمرنا فيهم فأتاه الأمر بقتالهم

NAHHAS:v4p249/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p249/r15.claim: The Prophet is not blameworthy before God for neglecting their warning, since he warned them and conveyed the message.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r15.anchor: ( فما أنت بملوم ) أي لا تلحقك لائمة من ربك جل وعز في تفريط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r3.claim: Turn away from excessive anguish over them, or from exhausting efforts to convert them: the Prophet has delivered the message and is not their controller.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r3.anchor: أي عن الحرص المفرط عليهم، وذهاب النفس حسرات،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r5.claim: If the instruction implies a truce, the sword verse abrogates all such truces.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r5.anchor: إلا في معنى الموادعة التي فيها، إن آية السيف نسخت جميع الموادعات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r3.claim: God tells Muhammad to turn away and assures him he is not blameworthy for doing so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r3.anchor: فأعرض عنهم يا محمد، {فما أنت بملوم

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r18.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r18.claim: Al-Dahhak says the order to turn away was superseded by the command to remind people, since Muhammad was later told to preach.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r18.anchor: والأول قول الضحاك لأنه قد أمر بالإقبال عليهم بالموعظة.

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r19.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r19.claim: Mujahid says God would not blame Muhammad for neglecting any duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r19.anchor: وقال مجاهد: { فتول عنهم } فأعرض عنهم { فما أنت بملوم } أي ليس يلومك ربك

ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r2.claim: There is no blame on the Prophet once he has delivered the message.
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r2.anchor: أي لا لوم عليك إذ أديت الرسالة

TABATABAI:51:52-56/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r5.claim: Because they persist arrogantly in argument and answer only with the old accusations, the Prophet should leave them without blame: he has shown the proof and completed the case.
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r5.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك ولم يجيبوا إلا بمثل قولهم ساحر أو مجنون ولم يزدهم دعوتك إلا عنادا فأعرض عنهم ولا تجادلهم

TABRISI:51:52-57/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:52-57/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:52-57/r3.claim: The Prophet should turn away after conveying the warning; blame for rejection belongs to the rejectors, not him.
TABRISI:51:52-57/r3.anchor: أي فأعرض عنهم يا محمد فقد بلغت وأنذرت

TABRISI:51:52-57/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:52-57/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:52-57/r4.claim: Commentators say the Prophet and believers grieved at the command, thinking revelation had stopped and punishment was imminent.
TABRISI:51:52-57/r4.anchor: حزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنون وظنوا أن الوحي قد انقطع

ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r17.claim: After repeating the summons and completing his duty, the Prophet may turn away from those who persist in stubborn transgression instead of continuing disputes.
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r17.anchor: Onun için sen şimdi onlardan yüz çevir

ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r18.claim: The Prophet is not blameworthy for turning away from them after fulfilling his duty.
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r18.anchor: O surette levm olunacak, kınanacak sen değilsin, sende kusur olmaz

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.claim: Every nation treated its messenger similarly, so the Prophet should patiently continue, turn from wrongdoers, and remind those who respond; God will support him and his companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.anchor: the same attitude was adopted by every nation towards their respective messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to turn away from the hostile people: he has warned and conveyed the truth, so he is not accountable for their rejection; they themselves are to blame.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r6.anchor: he has discharged his responsibility as a messenger of warning them and communicating to them the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r2.claim: The order to ignore applies to conceited Quraysh leaders unwilling to listen; the Prophet had pursued them because their conversion might strengthen the new faith and bring others to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r2.anchor: the directive of ignoring people relates to the rebellious leaders of the Quraysh who because of conceit were not prepared to listen to anything

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r3.claim: After the truth had been conclusively conveyed and the leaders proved immovable, God stopped the Prophet from spending more time pursuing them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p520/r3.anchor: when the truth had been conclusively conveyed to them, and it became evident that these rocks will not budge from their place

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p561/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p561/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p561/r1.claim: The Prophet should turn away from those repeatedly called who did not respond; he is not blameworthy after delivering and advising.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p561/r1.anchor: فتول عنهم: أي أعرض عن الذين كررت عليهم الدعوة، فلم يجيبوا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r3.claim: The Prophet may turn away because he delivered the message and did not fall short in his duty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r3.anchor: لا لوم عليك فقد أديت الرسالة وما قصرت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r4.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r4.claim: The exegetes say the command to turn away saddened the Prophet and distressed his Companions, who feared revelation had ceased and punishment was near; the command to remind them then reassured them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r4.anchor: المفسرون: لما نزلت هذه الآية حزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واشتد ذلك على أصحابه، وظنوا أن الوحي قد انقطع،

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r5.claim: After repeated calls meet only stubborn refusal, the Messenger should stop disputing; he is not blameworthy after doing his utmost to convey the message.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r5.anchor: فأعرض عن مجادلتهم بعدما كررت عليهم الدعوة فأبوا إلا الإصرار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r5.claim: After delivering the warning, the Prophet is told to turn away from further disputation and harsh confrontation; he is not blameworthy for their refusal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r5.anchor: كلف نفسك الإعراض عن الإبلاغ في إبلاغهم بالمجادلة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.claim: The question whether deniers taught one another their stance or are simply transgressive points to arrogance and darkened hearts as the common cause of their disbelief; God could have guided every soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.anchor: أي عجبا لهم يف جريهم على التكذيب والفساد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to turn away from them without blame.

ASAD-NOTES:51:54/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:54/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:51:54/r1.claim: The Prophet may turn away from his rejecters without blame.
ASAD-NOTES:51:54/r1.anchor: Turn, then, away from them, and thou shalt incur no blame

ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r1.claim: Turning away means ceasing to dispute after the Prophet repeatedly called them and spared no effort to clarify the truth, while they persisted in refusal and stubbornness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r1.anchor: فأعرض عن جدالهم فقد كررت عليهم الدعوة ولم تأل جهدا في البيان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r2.claim: After exhausting his effort and surpassing every known limit in conveying the message, the Prophet is not blameworthy for withdrawing.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20/r2.anchor: على التولي بعد ما بذلت المجهود وجاوزت في الأبلوغ كل حد معهود

ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God ordered Muhammad to withdraw so rejecters would be punished and excused him; the subsequent command to remind abrogated the withdrawal order.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r5.anchor: أمره الله تعالى أن يتولى عنهم ليعذبهم وعذر محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r6.claim: Ali says that when “turn away, you are not blamed” was revealed, believers feared destruction was certain; “and remind” then reassured them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p20#2/r6.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : لما نزلت

DURR-FULL:v7p624/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r1.claim: Ali says this command weighed heavily on the Companions: they feared divine anger and the end of revelation until the following command to remind them arrived; the reminder is with the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r1.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه في قوله {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} قال: ما نزلت علينا آية كانت أشد علينا منها ولا أعظم علينا منها

DURR-FULL:v7p624/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r2.claim: Qatada reports that the Companions feared revelation had stopped and punishment was imminent; God then revealed the command to remind.
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} قال: ذكر لنا أنها لما نزلت اشتد على أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p624/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r4.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet was first told to turn away from them, then to admonish them because reminders benefit believers.
DURR-FULL:v7p624/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} قال: فأعرض عنهم فقيل له: {وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين} فوعظهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3313#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3313#3/r1.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3313#3/r1.claim: Mujahid reports from Ali that when the Prophet was told to turn away, the Companions feared destruction until the following command to remind them was revealed, which reassured them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3313#3/r1.anchor: من طريق مجاهد ، عن علي قال : لما نزلت فتول عنهم فما انت بملوم لم يبق منا أحد الا ايقن بالهلكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r1.claim: Muhammad has conveyed the message and is therefore not blamed for turning away from them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r1.anchor: فقد بلغتهم فما أنت عليهم بملوم لأنك قد أديت الرسالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r2.claim: Most exegetes regard this verse as abrogated; the following segment reports two views about its abrogator.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#3/r2.anchor: ومذهب أكثر المفسرين أن هذه الآية منسوخة ولهم في ناسخها قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#4/r1.claim: Two views are given for what abrogates the preceding command: the next verse, or the verse of the sword.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#4/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه قوله وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين والثاني آية السيف

BURSEVI:v9p142/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p142/r1.claim: Youth, free time, and wealth can ruin a person; one should spend age, youth, and riches on the true aim.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r1.anchor: فعكسوا الأمر وكان ينبغي لهم أن يصرفوا العمر والشباب والغنى في تحصلي المطلوب الحقيقي

BURSEVI:v9p142/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p142/r2.claim: The cited Persian couplet presents love, youth, and revelry together as the desired set whose combination enables eloquent expression.

BURSEVI:v9p142/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p142/r3.claim: The outward command is to stop disputing after repeated invitations met only refusal and arrogance; the Persian gloss says to turn away from their requital until ordered to fight.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r3.anchor: فأعرض عن جدالهم فقد كررت عليهم الدعوة فأبوا إلا الاباء والاستكبار

BURSEVI:v9p142/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r4.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v9p142/r4.claim: Another explanation takes the command as turning away from excessive concern for them and grief that consumes the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r4.anchor: وفي فتح الرحمن فتول عن الحرص المفرط عليهم وذهاب النفس حسرات

BURSEVI:v9p142/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r5.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v9p142/r5.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the withdrawal as leaving them to the happiness or misery assigned to them in pre-eternity.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r5.anchor: وقال الواسطي ردهم إلى ما سبق عليهم في الأزل من السعادة والشقاوة

BURSEVI:v9p142/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p142/r6.claim: The Prophet is not censurable for withdrawing after exhausting his effort and exceeding every customary limit in conveying the message; malāma means censure.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r6.anchor: بذلت المجهود وجاوزت في الإبلاغ كل حد معهود

BURSEVI:v9p142/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p142/r7.claim: The word al-lawm and malāma mean reproach or censure, glossed in Persian as blame.

BURSEVI:v9p142/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r8.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p142/r8.claim: Some spiritual elders say the Prophet cannot guide those he loves; he conveys the message, while guidance is not his responsibility.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r8.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار فتول عنهم فإنك لا تهدي من احببت منهم

BURSEVI:v9p142/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p142/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p142/r9.claim: Another inward reading makes withdrawal a journey toward God: convey the message and means of salvation outwardly while remaining present to the divine Essence without being veiled.
BURSEVI:v9p142/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم فتول عنهم بسيرك إلينا فما أنت بملوم في إبلاغ رسالتك

MUJAHID:v2p621#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p621#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p621#2/r1.claim: Mujahid's address here is to Muhammad.
MUJAHID:v2p621#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد أي يا محمد

MUQATIL:51:54-55/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r1.claim: Muhammad should turn away from them: he has delivered the message and discharged his duty, so he is not blameworthy.
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r1.anchor: يعني فأعرض عنهم، فقد بلغت وأعذرت { فمآ أنت } يا محمد { بملوم }

MUQATIL:51:54-55/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r2.claim: The Prophet grieved, fearing punishment would descend upon them, and God then commanded him to remind them.
MUQATIL:51:54-55/r2.anchor: { فمآ أنت } يا محمد { بملوم } [آية: 54] يقول: فلا تلام، فحزن النبي صلىالله عليه وسلم مخافة أن ينزل بهم العذاب، فأنزل الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r1.claim: Turn away from those who repeatedly received the call but stubbornly did not respond.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r1.anchor: فاعرض عن الذين كررت عليهم الدعوة فلم يجيبوا اعتادا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r2.claim: You are not blameworthy for turning away after delivering the message and exhausting your effort in proclamation and invitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#10/r2.anchor: فلا لوم عليك فى اعراضك بعد ما بلغت الرسالة وبذلت مجهودك في البلاغ والدعوة

RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r1.claim: From noble character, the Prophet blamed his own shortcoming for their unbelief and therefore intensified his warning and conveying of the message.
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r1.anchor: هذه تسلية أخرى ، وذلك لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان من كرم الأخلاق

RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r2.claim: God reassures the Prophet that he fulfilled his duty; their rejection is not his fault, and their turning away and stubbornness make them culpable.
RAZI-FULL:v28p198/r2.anchor: قد أتيت بما عليك ، ولا يضرك التولي عنهم ، وكفرهم ليس لتقصير منك

STUDYQURAN:51:54/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r1.claim: After delivering the message, the Prophet is not accountable for whether disbelievers follow it or for their punishment if they refuse.
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r1.anchor: you are not responsible for whether the disbelievers follow it or for the punishment that will afflict them if they do not

STUDYQURAN:51:54/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r2.claim: His continuing responsibility is to remind believers, who benefit from the message.
STUDYQURAN:51:54/r2.anchor: you are only responsible to continue reminding the believers who do benefit from the message

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to turn away from Quraysh's polytheists until God's command concerning them comes.

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r2.claim: The verb waliya here means to turn away from and leave someone.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r2.anchor: كما قال حصين بن ضمضم: أما بنو عبس فإن هجينهم … ولى فوارسه وأفلت أعورا

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r3.speaker: حصين بن ضمضم
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r3.claim: Husayn ibn Damdam's verse uses waliya for a party turning away, and describes aʿwar as someone who failed to achieve his aim.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r3.anchor: كما قال حصين بن ضمضم: أما بنو عبس فإن هجينهم … ولى فوارسه وأفلت أعورا

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r4.claim: In the cited verse, aʿwar describes one whose need was unmet and who did not attain what he sought.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r4.anchor: والأعور في هذا الموضع: الذي عور فلم تقض حاجته، ولم يصب ما طلب

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the command as turn away from them.

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r6.claim: God will not reproach Muhammad for neglecting the warning, because he warned them and delivered his commission.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r6.anchor: لا يلومك ربك على تفريط كان منك في الإنذار، فقد أنذرت، وبلغت ما أرسلت به

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r7.claim: Mujahid identifies the addressee of the statement as Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r7.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} [الذاريات: 54] قال: «محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad delivered what he was sent with, so he is not blameworthy; one cannot blame him after he fulfilled the command.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} [الذاريات: 54] قال: «قد بلغت ما أرسلناك به، فلست بملوم» قال: «وكيف يلومه، وقد أدى ما أمر به»

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r9.claim: Qatada says the companions feared revelation had ceased and punishment was imminent when told to withdraw; the following command to remind them then came.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r9.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} [الذاريات: 54] " ذكر لنا أنها لما نزلت هذه الآية، اشتد على أصحاب رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v21p551/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r10.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r10.claim: Ali relates that the companions were saddened and thought the Messenger had been ordered to leave them until the reminder command was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v21p551/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: خرج علي معتجرا ببرد، مشتملا بخميصة، فقال " لما نزلت {فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم} [الذاريات: 54] أحزننا ذلك وقلنا

SULAMI:v2p277#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r1.claim: Sahl reads the command as turning away because the Prophet has exerted himself in conveying the message.
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : اعرض عنهم فقد جهدت بالإبلاغ .

SULAMI:v2p277#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says to leave them to their eternal decree of felicity or misery; the verse removes blame from the Prophet because he counselled, strove, and suffered.
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ذرهم إلى ما سبق عليهم في الأزل من السعادة والشقاوة وإسقاط الملامة عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

SULAMI:v2p277#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata hears God inviting the Prophet to return to Him and assuring him that he has not fallen short in his charge.
SULAMI:v2p277#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ارجع إلينا فما قصرت فيما امرت .

TUSTARI:51:54/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:51:54/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:51:54/r1.claim: The Prophet is to turn away from them because he has exhausted his effort in conveying the message.
TUSTARI:51:54/r1.anchor: أعرض عنهم فقد جهدت في الإبلاغ جهدك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is to turn away from the polytheists after delivering the warning; he is not blameworthy because he conveyed the message.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r1.anchor: يقول: فأعرض عن هؤلاء المشركين فقد بلغت وأنذرت، وهو قوله: {فما أنت بملوم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet feared punishment would descend on his people; Muqatil and Qatada agree, and the Companions feared revelation had stopped and punishment was imminent before the command to remind came.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فحزن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- لما نزلت هذه الآية مخافة أن تنزل بقومه العذاب.
